rules.title: CTA Hierarchy
rules.description: One decision is clear on the first screen. Objective check: count the filled calls to action with different labels in the first screen (4 or more needs a person) and any call-to-action label repeated 6 or more times on the page.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Evaluate ONLY this rule: "CTA Hierarchy". Identify competing actions that obscure the intended decision. Use only the supplied page context. Quote the exact words or elements you rely on. If the context is not enough to decide, answer "inconclusive". If the rule does not apply to this page, answer "not_applicable".
rules.recommendationTemplate: Choose the one action you want most and make it the only filled button on the first screen; make the others plain links. Found: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: Several equally loud buttons leave the visitor unsure which to press. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Competing actions split attention and can lower clicks on the one that matters. This is a hypothesis; Avara did not measure conversions.
